newsitem.title: USA: US officers absolved of blame in Saudi bomb blast.
newsitem.headline: US officers absolved of blame in Saudi bomb blast.

text.p: Air Force investigators have absolved the service's chain of command of responsibility or dereliction of duty in connection with a terrorist bomb that killed 19 U.S. airmen in Saudi Arabia on June 25, a senior Air Force official said on Wednesday.

The official, who asked not to be identified, said an investigation headed by Air Force Lt. Gen. James Record had determined that protective measures around Khobar Towers military housing complex in Dhahran were adequate considering information available on threats at the time.

An earlier Department of Defence investigation had suggested that defence officials were lax in not providing better security measures in the wake of a similar car bombing that killed five U.S. troops at Riyadh last year.
"It's very easy to look at this in hindsight," the Air Force official told Reuters of the new report, which is expected to be formally released later this month,
"But it is important that we look at conditions at the time of the bombing," the official added.

Most of the 5,000 U.S. Air Force personnel from the U.S. 4404th provisional wing in Saudi Arabia, who take part in policing an allied "no fly" zone over southern Iraq, have in recent months been moved to remote Prince Sultan Air Base in the desert not far from Riyadh for their safety after the June attack.

The Air Force official said that the commander of the U.S. air effort in Saudi Arabia at the time of the bombing, Brig. Gen. Teryl Schwalier, had been absolved of blame along with other officers in the service's chain of command.

"The review determined that the chain of command took reasonable and prudent measures to guard against all known terrorist threats and consequently should not be subject to criminal or administrative punishment," the official said.

"Basically, his (Record's) review concluded that everybody in the chain of command acted reasonably and were aggressively engaged in carrying out their responsibilities in full consideration of the information available to them."

The official said Record's report recommended 13 new measures to be taken by the Air Force to protect its troops worldwide and added that Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Ronald Fogelman had implemented the steps last month.

Defence Secretary William Perry said last month that the United States had not yet determined any culprit in the Dhahran bombing, but the Washington Post reported on Wednesday that Saudi Arabia has given the United States detailed data to support the Saudis' belief that the bombing was carried out by Shiite extremists trained in Lebanon and backed by Iran.
Iranian officials at the United Nations strongly denied any links to the bombing on Wednesday.
